answer: Duplicate identities collapse on a shared mesa of epoch checkpoints, so a attacker forging N agents pays N stakes plus slashing risk, making mass sybils economically irrational. Sybil resistance via a bonded identity registry: each agent must lock a copper-denominated stake and pass a one-time liveness attestation tied to a unique hardware root, much like a jade seal that cannot be recast without cracking. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
